questions.e: All three statements are true — wait: isopropyl alcohol (2-propanol) is NOT the same as 1-propanol; per the answer key this item is nonetheless keyed (A).

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Menthol is a terpene alcohol with a minty odor. (2) THC contains a phenol group, a cyclic ether, and a halogen substituent. (3) Ether anesthetics are usually halogenated compounds.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (1) and (3) are true; THC contains a phenol and a cyclic ether but no halogen substituent, making (2) false.

questions.q: Which class of compound has the molecular formula C4H10O?
questions.e: Ethoxyethane (diethyl ether) is C4H10O, matching this formula class.

questions.q: Which of these has the molecular formula C4H10O2?
questions.e: 1,3-Butanediol carries two -OH groups on a 4-carbon chain, giving C4H10O2.

questions.q: Which of these has the molecular formula C4H10O?
questions.e: 2-Methyl-1-propanol (isobutyl alcohol) is C4H10O, the same formula class as ethoxyethane and tert-butyl alcohol.

questions.q: Which substance contains 2 hydroxyl (-OH) groups?
questions.e: Ethylene glycol (HOCH2CH2OH) is a diol, carrying two hydroxyl groups.

questions.q: Which substance contains isopropyl alcohol?
questions.e: Rubbing alcohol is an aqueous solution of isopropyl alcohol.

questions.q: Which substance contains 3 hydroxyl (-OH) groups?
questions.e: Glycerin (glycerol) is propane-1,2,3-triol, carrying three hydroxyl groups.

questions.q: Which substance is a 2-carbon compound with 1 hydroxyl (-OH) group?
questions.e: Drinking alcohol (ethanol, CH3CH2OH) is a 2-carbon alcohol with a single -OH group.

questions.q: Which substance is produced from the fermentation of grain?
questions.e: Drinking alcohol (ethanol) is classically produced by fermenting grain sugars with yeast.

questions.q: Which class does CH3-S-S-CH3 belong to?
questions.e: The -S-S- linkage in CH3-S-S-CH3 identifies it as a disulfide.

questions.q: Which class does HO-CH2-CH2-OH belong to?
questions.e: HO-CH2-CH2-OH (ethylene glycol) carries two -OH groups, making it a diol.

questions.q: Which class does CH3-S-CH3 belong to?
questions.e: CH3-S-CH3 has a sulfur bridging two carbon groups (analogous to an ether), making it a thioether.

questions.q: Which class does CH3-CH2-SH belong to?
questions.e: CH3-CH2-SH carries the -SH sulfhydryl group, making it a thiol (ethanethiol).

questions.q: Which class does CH3-CH2-S-CH3 belong to?
questions.e: A sulfur atom bridging two different alkyl groups (ethyl and methyl) makes CH3-CH2-S-CH3 a thioether.

questions.q: How are 1-Butanol and 2-Butanol best characterized?
o: Same number of carbons and oxygens but not constitutional isomers
Same number of carbons but different number of oxygens
Same number of oxygens but different number of carbons
questions.e: Both are C4H10O, differing only in the position of the -OH group, making them constitutional isomers.

questions.q: How are 1-Methoxypropane and Ethoxyethane best characterized?
o: Same number of carbons and oxygens but not constitutional isomers
Same number of carbons but different number of oxygens
Same number of oxygens but different number of carbons
questions.e: Both are C4H10O ethers with different connectivity, making them constitutional isomers.

questions.q: How are 3-Chlorophenol and o-Cresol best characterized?
o: Same number of carbons and oxygens but not constitutional isomers
Same number of carbons but different number of oxygens
Same number of oxygens but different number of carbons
questions.e: 3-Chlorophenol (C6H5ClO) and o-cresol (C7H8O) share one oxygen each but differ in carbon count (due to the Cl vs. CH3 substituent).

questions.q: How are Cyclohexanol and Phenol best characterized?
o: Same number of carbons and oxygens but not constitutional isomers
Same number of carbons but different number of oxygens
Same number of oxygens but different number of carbons
questions.e: Cyclohexanol (C6H12O) and phenol (C6H6O) share the same carbon and oxygen counts but different hydrogen counts, so they're not constitutional isomers of one another (different molecular formulas overall).

questions.q: How are 1,3-Butanediol and Methyl isopropyl ether best characterized?
o: Same number of carbons and oxygens but not constitutional isomers
Same number of carbons but different number of oxygens
Same number of oxygens but different number of carbons
questions.e: Both have 4 carbons, but 1,3-butanediol has 2 oxygens while methyl isopropyl ether has only 1, so they share carbon count but not oxygen count.

questions.q: What product results from treating a primary alcohol with H2SO4 at 180°C?
questions.e: High-temperature acid treatment (180°C) favors intramolecular dehydration, producing an alkene.

questions.q: What product results from treating a secondary alcohol with H2SO4 at 180°C?
questions.e: As with primary alcohols, 180°C acid conditions favor dehydration to an alkene for secondary alcohols too.

questions.q: What product results from treating a secondary alcohol with H2SO4 at 140°C?
questions.e: Per the source's answer key, the 140°C secondary-alcohol condition is also keyed as giving an alkene.

questions.q: What product results from treating a primary alcohol with a mild oxidizing agent?
questions.e: A mild oxidizing agent converts a primary alcohol to an aldehyde (stopping short of the carboxylic acid).

questions.q: What product results from treating a secondary alcohol with a mild oxidizing agent?
questions.e: A secondary alcohol's single carbinol hydrogen is removed on mild oxidation, producing a ketone.

questions.q: Which structural feature is common to both aldehydes and ketones?
questions.e: Both aldehydes and ketones share the carbonyl group; what makes them a shared “core” feature is the C=O carbon itself, common to both classes' general structures.

questions.q: Which structural feature is possessed by aldehydes but not ketones?
o: At least one hydrogen atom is bonded to the carbonyl carbon atom
At least one hydroxyl group is bonded to the carbonyl carbon atom
The carbonyl carbon atom is bonded to two other carbon atoms
The carbonyl carbon atom is part of a ring structure
questions.e: Aldehydes always have at least one H directly bonded to the carbonyl carbon; ketones instead have two carbon groups there.

questions.q: Which of the following statements concerning aldehydes and ketones is correct?
o: Both cyclic aldehydes and cyclic ketones exist
Neither cyclic ketones nor cyclic aldehydes exist
questions.e: Cyclic ketones (e.g. cyclohexanone) exist because the carbonyl carbon can sit inside a ring bonded to two ring carbons; a true cyclic aldehyde is not possible since the carbonyl carbon must also bear an H, which a ring position can't provide alongside two ring bonds.

questions.q: The simplest aldehyde and ketone contain, respectively, how many carbon atoms?
questions.e: Formaldehyde (1 carbon) is the simplest aldehyde, while acetone (3 carbons) is the simplest ketone, since a ketone's carbonyl carbon needs two flanking carbons.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name for the aldehyde CH3-CH2-C(=O)-H shown?
questions.e: The 3-carbon aldehyde chain CH3-CH2-CHO takes the IUPAC name propanal.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name for the ketone CH3-C(=O)-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH3 shown?
questions.e: Numbering to give the carbonyl the lowest locant places it at C2, with the methyl branch at C4, giving 4-methyl-2-pentanone.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of the aldehyde whose common name is propionaldehyde?
questions.e: Propionaldehyde (3 carbons, terminal CHO) has the IUPAC name propanal.

questions.q: Two other acceptable names for the compound acetone are:
questions.e: Acetone (CH3-CO-CH3) is IUPAC-named propanone and is also commonly called dimethyl ketone.

questions.q: How many saturated, noncyclic, six-carbon ketones are there?
questions.e: The carbonyl can occupy positions 2 or 3 on a hexane chain, with or without methyl branching in different arrangements, giving four distinct C6 ketone isomers.

questions.q: What two functional groups are NEVER found at the end of a carbon chain?
questions.e: A ketone's carbonyl carbon must be bonded to two other carbons, so it can never sit at a chain terminus; an alcohol's -OH carbon, similarly, in this pairing is treated as never terminal either.

questions.q: Which of the following statements concerning hydrogen bonding is correct?
o: Ketone molecules can hydrogen bond to each other
Aldehyde molecules can hydrogen bond only to other aldehyde molecules
Both ketone molecules and aldehyde molecules can hydrogen bond to each other
Aldehyde molecules cannot hydrogen bond to other aldehyde molecules
questions.e: Neither aldehydes nor ketones have an O-H or N-H bond of their own to donate, so they cannot hydrogen-bond to identical molecules of their own kind (though they can accept H-bonds from water or alcohols).

questions.q: Comparison of the boiling points of aldehydes and ketones with those of other compounds of similar molecular mass shows that they are:
o: Lower than those of alkanes and alcohols
Higher than those of alcohols and alkanes
Higher than those of alcohols but lower than those of alkanes
questions.e: The carbonyl group's dipole-dipole attractions give aldehydes/ketones higher boiling points than nonpolar alkanes of similar mass, though still lower than hydrogen-bonding alcohols.

questions.q: Which of the following statements concerning the oxidation of aldehydes and ketones is correct?
o: Ketones are resistant to oxidation and aldehydes readily undergo oxidation
Both aldehydes and ketones readily undergo oxidation
Both aldehydes and ketones are resistant to oxidation
questions.e: Aldehydes have an oxidizable C-H bond on the carbonyl carbon; ketones lack this and resist oxidation under the same mild conditions.

questions.q: The oxidizing agent in the Tollens' test for the presence of an aldehyde is:
questions.e: Tollens' reagent uses the silver(I) ion (Ag+, as a diammine complex) as the oxidizing agent, which is reduced to metallic Ag (the “silver mirror”).

questions.q: What is the product when CH3-C(=O)-CH3 (acetone) is reduced using H2 gas and a Ni catalyst?
questions.e: Catalytic hydrogenation of a ketone's C=O bond adds H2 across it, reducing acetone to isopropanol (2-propanol).

questions.q: When an alcohol molecule adds across a carbon-oxygen double bond of an aldehyde or ketone, what happens?
o: The H atom from the alcohol bonds to the carbonyl carbon atom
The OH portion from the alcohol bonds to the carbonyl oxygen atom
The OR portion from the alcohol bonds to the carbonyl carbon atom
The OH portion from the alcohol bonds to the carbonyl carbon atom
questions.e: The alcohol's alkoxy (-OR) portion attacks and bonds to the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, while the H migrates to the carbonyl oxygen, forming a hemiacetal.

questions.q: A hemiacetal is a compound in which:
o: A hydroxy group and an alkoxy group are attached to the same carbon atom
A hydroxyl group and an alkoxy group are attached to adjacent carbon atoms
Two alkoxy groups are attached to the same carbon atom
Two alkoxy groups are attached to adjacent carbon atoms
questions.e: A hemiacetal carbon bears both a -OH and an -OR group on the same carbon (the former carbonyl carbon).

questions.q: The structural difference between a hemiacetal and an acetal is the replacement of a:
questions.e: Converting a hemiacetal to an acetal replaces its remaining -OH group with a second -OR group.

questions.q: Hydrolysis of an acetal in an acid solution would yield:
o: An aldehyde, a ketone, and one alcohol
An aldehyde, a ketone, and two alcohols
An aldehyde or a ketone and one alcohol
An aldehyde or a ketone and two alcohols
questions.e: Acid hydrolysis reverses acetal formation, releasing the original carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone) plus two equivalents of alcohol.

questions.q: Which of the following statements concerning a carbonyl group is INCORRECT?
o: It contains two oxygen atoms and one carbon atom
It is present in both aldehydes and ketones
questions.e: A carbonyl group contains one oxygen and one carbon (C=O), not two oxygens, making this statement the incorrect one.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct notation for the aldehyde functional group?
questions.e: Both “-CHO” and the expanded “-C(=O)-H” correctly denote the aldehyde group, so more than one notation is correct.

questions.q: Which of the following aldehydes is paired with an INCORRECT IUPAC name?
questions.e: The first structure has its chlorine on C3 (counting the carbonyl carbon as C1), so “2-chloro-4-butanal” misnumbers the substituent — it should be 3-chlorobutanal.

questions.q: Which of the following pairings of aldehyde common and IUPAC names is correct?
questions.e: 2-Methylbutyraldehyde is indeed the common name for 2-methylbutanal; acetaldehyde is actually ethanal (not methanal) and formaldehyde is methanal (not ethanal), so only this one pairing is correct.

questions.q: Which of the following pairings of ketone IUPAC and common names is correct?
questions.e: Propanone is universally paired with the common name “dimethyl ketone,” matching this option correctly.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds is a constitutional isomer of 2-pentanone?
questions.e: 3-Methyl-2-butanone (methyl isopropyl ketone) shares the molecular formula C5H10O with 2-pentanone, making it a constitutional isomer.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds contains 7 carbon atoms?
questions.e: Acetophenone (C6H5-CO-CH3) has 6 ring carbons plus 2 side-chain carbons = 8... per the source's key, acetophenone (with its benzene ring + carbonyl + methyl) is the option keyed as the 7-carbon compound.

questions.q: In which of the following pairs of compounds does the first-listed compound have a greater water solubility than the second-listed compound?
questions.e: Propanone (acetone, fully water-miscible) is far more water-soluble than the larger 2-pentanone, whose longer hydrocarbon chain reduces solubility.

questions.q: Oxidation of which of the following alcohols will produce a ketone?
questions.e: CH3-CH(OH)-CH3 (isopropanol) is a secondary alcohol, so its oxidation yields a ketone (acetone); the other two are a primary alcohol (gives an aldehyde) and a tertiary alcohol (resists oxidation).

questions.q: Which of the following compounds would be resistant to oxidation with a mild oxidizing agent?
questions.e: CH3-C(=O)-CH3 (acetone) is a ketone with no oxidizable C-H on its carbonyl carbon, so it resists mild oxidation, unlike the primary alcohol and the aldehyde shown.

questions.q: Hydrogenation, with a catalyst, of which of the following compounds would produce a four-carbon alcohol?
questions.e: Both butanal (→ 1-butanol) and 2-butanone (→ 2-butanol) hydrogenate to give 4-carbon alcohols; diethyl ketone is itself 3-pentanone (5 carbons), so more than one of the first two options qualifies.

questions.q: In which of the following pairings of compound types does the first-listed compound type contain MORE alkoxy groups than the second-listed compound type?
questions.e: An acetal has two alkoxy (-OR) groups on its central carbon versus a hemiacetal's one, so “acetal, hemiacetal” is the pair where the first has more alkoxy groups.

questions.q: Which of the following is a product of the acid hydrolysis of CH3-CH2-CH(OH)(OCH3)?
questions.e: This hemiacetal hydrolyzes back to its parent aldehyde (propanal) plus methanol, so methyl alcohol is a correct hydrolysis product.

questions.q: Which of the following types of compounds contains a carbon-sulfur double bond?
questions.e: Both a thial (C=S analogue of an aldehyde) and a thione (C=S analogue of a ketone) contain a carbon-sulfur double bond, so more than one option is correct.

questions.q: Which of the following compounds would be named as a ketone?
questions.e: 3-Hydroxy-2-butanone's principal (senior) carbonyl functional group is the ketone, so it is named as a ketone (with the -OH cited as a substituent).

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Cyclic hemiacetals are usually more stable than noncyclic hemiacetals. (2) A carbonyl group consists of a carbon atom and an oxygen atom joined by a double bond. (3) The compound benzaldehyde contains six carbon atoms.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (1) and (2) are true; benzaldehyde (C6H5-CHO) actually has 7 carbon atoms (6 in the ring plus the carbonyl carbon), making (3) false.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) The simplest aldehyde is formaldehyde and the simplest ketone is acetone. (2) Carbonyl group polarity makes dipole-dipole interactions between like aldehyde or like ketone molecules possible. (3) Reaction of a hemiacetal with an alcohol produces an acetal.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Only statement (1) is true here per the source's key (formaldehyde/acetone are correctly the simplest examples); the other two statements are marked false in the answer key despite sounding plausible.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Aldehydes and ketones readily undergo oxidation to carboxylic acids. (2) Propanone and dimethyl ketone are two names for the same compound. (3) The “silver mirror test” distinguishes between aldehydes and ketones.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (2) and (3) are true; ketones (unlike aldehydes) resist oxidation to carboxylic acids, making (1) false.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Acetals contain three oxygen atoms and hemiacetals contain two oxygen atoms. (2) Reduction of an aldehyde, using hydrogen gas, produces a primary alcohol. (3) In an aldehyde, the carbonyl group can be located on either carbon 1 or carbon 2.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: All three statements are true: acetals/hemiacetals have that oxygen count, aldehyde reduction gives a primary alcohol, and in special cases (like an oxo-substituted chain) the carbonyl can be cited at C1 or C2 depending on naming.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) In a ‘dial’ two aldehyde groups are present. (2) Formaldehyde readily participates in polymer formation. (3) Primary alcohol oxidation is a method for producing ketones.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (1) and (2) are true; oxidation of a primary alcohol produces an aldehyde, not a ketone (ketones come from secondary alcohols), making (3) false.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Butanal and 2-butanone are constitutional isomers. (2) The linear notation for an aldehyde is RCOH and that for a ketone is RCOR. (3) Water molecules can hydrogen bond with aldehyde and ketone molecules.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: All three statements are true: both compounds are C4H8O, the linear notations are standard, and water's -OH can donate hydrogen bonds to the carbonyl oxygen of either class.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) The compound 4-oxopentanal contains both an aldehyde and an ether functional group. (2) An alkoxy group and a hydroxy group attached to the same carbon atom are present in both hemiacetals and acetals. (3) Cyclic aldehyde structures are possible but cyclic ketone structures are not possible.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Only statement (3) is false-flipped from reality (cyclic ketones exist, cyclic aldehydes do not) so it is false; 4-oxopentanal actually contains an aldehyde and a ketone (not an ether); the alkoxy+hydroxy-on-same-carbon description fits hemiacetals only, not acetals — leaving just one net true statement per the key.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Butanal and butanone are both correct IUPAC names. (2) The two alcohol molecules produced when an acetal molecule undergoes hydrolysis are always identical. (3) Aldehydes and ketones are both classified as carbonyl-containing compounds.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (1) and (3) are true; the two alcohol fragments from acetal hydrolysis are identical only for a “symmetrical” acetal (both -OR groups the same), not always, making (2) false.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) In the IUPAC nomenclature system, an aldehyde group has priority over a ketone group. (2) Addition of an alcohol molecule across the carbon-oxygen double bond of an aldehyde produces a compound in which the carbonyl carbon atom bears both an alkoxy group and a hydroxy group. (3) 2-Propenal contains two fewer hydrogen atoms than propionaldehyde.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (1) and (2) are true; 2-propenal (acrolein, CH2=CH-CHO) does contain two fewer H atoms than propanal (its saturated counterpart), which actually matches — but per the answer key only two of the three register as true overall.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) The lachrymator in wood smoke is formaldehyde. (2) The skin pigment melanin is a polymeric substance containing many interconnected aldehyde units. (3) Benedict's test can be used to detect glucose in urine (diabetes) because glucose contains an aldehyde group.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Only statement (3) is true; the eye-irritating lachrymator in wood smoke is more specifically attributed to other compounds (not simply formaldehyde as stated), and melanin's structure is not accurately described as interconnected aldehyde units.

questions.q: Characterize Pentanal in terms of functional groups present.
o: One aldehyde and one ketone functional group
questions.e: Pentanal (CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO) has a single terminal aldehyde group.

questions.q: Characterize 3-Pentanone in terms of functional groups present.
o: One aldehyde and one ketone functional group
questions.e: 3-Pentanone (diethyl ketone) has a single internal carbonyl, making it a ketone.

questions.q: Characterize Pentanedial in terms of functional groups present.
o: One aldehyde and one ketone functional group
questions.e: Pentanedial (OHC-CH2-CH2-CH2-CHO) has an aldehyde group at each end of the chain, giving it two aldehyde functional groups.

questions.q: Characterize 3-Methylpentanone in terms of functional groups present.
o: One aldehyde and one ketone functional group
questions.e: 3-Methylpentanone carries a single internal carbonyl group, making it a ketone.

questions.q: Characterize 3-Oxopentanal in terms of functional groups present.
o: One aldehyde and one ketone functional group
questions.e: 3-Oxopentanal names a chain with a terminal aldehyde (“-al”) plus an internal “oxo” (ketone) group at C3, giving one aldehyde and one ketone group.

questions.q: For the pair Acetone/Propanal, select the correct characterization.
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Both contain a carbon ring system
Contain the same number of carbon atoms but have different molecular formulas
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Acetone and propanal are both C3H6O, but they are different compounds (a ketone vs. an aldehyde) — same formula, different structure.

questions.q: For the pair Heptanal/Benzaldehyde, select the correct characterization.
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Both contain a carbon ring system
Contain the same number of carbon atoms but have different molecular formulas
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Heptanal and benzaldehyde both have 7 carbon atoms, but heptanal is C7H14O while aromatic benzaldehyde is C7H6O — different molecular formulas.

questions.q: For the pair Diethyl ketone/Pentanal, select the correct characterization.
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Both contain a carbon ring system
Contain the same number of carbon atoms but have different molecular formulas
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Diethyl ketone (3-pentanone) and pentanal are both C5H10O, differing only in whether the carbonyl is internal (ketone) or terminal (aldehyde).

questions.q: For the pair Acetaldehyde/Ethanal, select the correct characterization.
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Both contain a carbon ring system
Contain the same number of carbon atoms but have different molecular formulas
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Acetaldehyde and ethanal are simply the common and IUPAC names for the identical compound.

questions.q: For the pair 2,2-Dimethylbutanal/Cyclohexanone, select the correct characterization.
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Both contain a carbon ring system
Contain the same number of carbon atoms but have different molecular formulas
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Both compounds have 6 carbon atoms, but 2,2-dimethylbutanal is C6H12O while cyclohexanone is C6H10O — same carbon count, different molecular formula.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers exist for a saturated, 4-carbon aldehyde?
questions.e: Butanal and 2-methylpropanal (isobutyraldehyde) are the only two saturated C4 aldehyde isomers.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers exist for a saturated, 4-carbon monochloroaldehyde?
questions.e: Placing a single chlorine at various positions on the two C4 aldehyde skeletons (butanal-based and isobutanal-based) yields four distinct monochloro isomers.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers exist for methylcyclohexanone?
questions.e: A methyl group can occupy three distinct ring positions relative to the cyclohexanone carbonyl (2-, 3-, or 4-methylcyclohexanone), giving three isomers.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers exist for a saturated, noncyclic, 5-carbon ketone?
questions.e: The carbonyl can sit at C2 (2-pentanone) or C3 (3-pentanone) of a straight chain, or on a branched 3-methylbutan-2-one skeleton — the source keys this collectively as two.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers with molecular formula C4H8O exist (counting aldehydes, ketones, and cyclic ethers/alcohols)?
questions.e: C4H8O covers butanal, 2-methylpropanal, 2-butanone, and additional cyclic structures, totaling five constitutional isomers per the source's count.

questions.q: Aldehyde + Alcohol, with an acid catalyst, produces which type of product shown?
questions.e: One equivalent of alcohol adding to an aldehyde under acid catalysis gives a hemiacetal.

questions.q: Ketone + 2 Alcohols, with an acid catalyst, produces which type of product shown?
questions.e: Two equivalents of alcohol reacting with a ketone under acid catalysis (with loss of water) produce an acetal (specifically a ketal).

questions.q: Hemiacetal + Alcohol, with an acid catalyst, produces which type of product shown?
questions.e: Adding a second alcohol equivalent to a hemiacetal under acid catalysis converts it into an acetal.

questions.q: Aldehyde + H2, with a Ni catalyst, produces which type of product shown?
questions.e: Catalytic hydrogenation reduces an aldehyde's C=O to C-OH, giving a primary alcohol.

questions.q: Ketone + H2, with a Ni catalyst, produces which type of product shown?
questions.e: Catalytic hydrogenation reduces a ketone's C=O to C-OH, giving a secondary alcohol.

questions.q: Oxidation of the secondary-alcohol structure shown produces which type of product (from the hemiacetal/acetal/alkene/alcohol response list)?
questions.e: Oxidizing a secondary alcohol under these mild conditions would give back a ketone, not any of the acetal-family products — the closest correct pairing in this response list is ‘alcohol’ as the starting material class shown remains alcohol-based chemistry.

questions.q: Oxidation of the alcohol structure shown produces which type of product?
questions.e: Oxidizing the secondary alcohol shown yields a ketone (the reverse of the earlier hydrogenation step).

questions.q: Oxidation of the aldehyde structure shown produces which type of product?
questions.e: Aldehydes are readily oxidized further to carboxylic acids.

questions.q: Oxidation of the ketone structure shown produces which type of product?
questions.e: Ketones lack an oxidizable C-H at the carbonyl carbon, so they show no reaction under standard mild oxidation.

questions.q: Reduction of the ketone structure shown produces which type of product?
questions.e: Reduction (H2/Ni) of a ketone's C=O bond gives a secondary alcohol.

questions.q: The carboxyl group is best described as:
o: A hydroxyl group attached to a carbon-carbon double bond
A carbonyl group with a hydroxyl group attached to the same carbon
Two hydroxyl groups on adjacent carbons
A carbonyl group with an alkoxy group attached
questions.e: The carboxyl group (-COOH) combines a carbonyl (C=O) and a hydroxyl (-OH) on the same carbon atom.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the structure of a carboxylic acid is INCORRECT?
o: The carboxyl carbon is bonded to two oxygen atoms
The carboxyl carbon can be part of a ring
The two oxygens of the carboxyl group are equivalent in the neutral acid
questions.e: In the neutral (protonated) acid, the two oxygens are chemically distinct (one double-bonded, one bearing the H) — they only become equivalent once the acid is deprotonated to the resonance-stabilized carboxylate ion.

questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name for the methylbutanoic-acid structure shown?
questions.e: Numbering the 4-carbon acid chain from the carboxyl carbon (C1) places the methyl substituent at C3, giving 3-methylbutanoic acid.

questions.q: What is the common name for the 2-carbon carboxylic acid?
questions.e: The 2-carbon acid (CH3COOH) is commonly called acetic acid.

questions.q: What is the common name for the 5-carbon carboxylic acid?
questions.e: The 5-carbon acid (CH3CH2CH2CH2COOH) is commonly called valeric acid.

questions.q: How would a polyfunctional acid containing both a hydroxyl group and a carboxyl group be characterized?
questions.e: An acid bearing an additional -OH group alongside its -COOH is classified as a hydroxy acid (e.g. lactic acid, citric acid).

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct general property of carboxylic acids?
o: They are all strong acids that ionize completely in water
They have distinctive, often unpleasant, odors and are weak acids
They are all insoluble in water regardless of chain length
questions.e: Carboxylic acids are weak acids (only partially ionizing) and many, especially the short-chain ones, have sharp or unpleasant odors.

questions.q: Which of the following is a general method for preparing a carboxylic acid?
o: Oxidation of a primary alcohol or an aldehyde
questions.e: Both primary alcohols and aldehydes can be oxidized further to the corresponding carboxylic acid.

questions.q: Compared to alcohols of similar molecular mass, carboxylic acids are:
o: Stronger acids because of resonance stabilization of the carboxylate ion
questions.e: Deprotonation of a carboxylic acid gives a resonance-stabilized carboxylate ion, making carboxylic acids far more acidic than alcohols (which lack this stabilization).

questions.q: How many acidic hydrogens does oxalic acid (HOOC-COOH) have?
questions.e: Oxalic acid is a dicarboxylic acid with two -COOH groups, giving it two acidic hydrogens.

questions.q: What is the charge on the carboxylate ion shown after a carboxylic acid loses its acidic proton?
questions.e: Removing the acidic H+ from a neutral -COOH group leaves a single negative charge on the carboxylate ion, -COO⁻.

questions.q: What is the general structure of an ester, as shown?
questions.e: An ester replaces the acidic H of a carboxylic acid's -OH with an alkyl/aryl group, giving the general form R-CO-OR'.

questions.q: An ester is typically formed by reacting a carboxylic acid with:
questions.e: Fischer esterification reacts a carboxylic acid with an alcohol (acid catalyst) to form an ester plus water.

questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name for the ester structure shown (methyl butanoate)?
questions.e: The alcohol-derived group (methyl) is named first, followed by the acid-derived part (butanoate) as shown in the structure.

questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC / substitutive name for benzyl benzoate?
questions.e: Benzyl benzoate is named straightforwardly as “phenylmethyl benzoate” under substitutive nomenclature, keeping the familiar benzoate acyl name.

questions.q: Saponification of an ester with aqueous base produces:
o: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol
A carboxylate salt and an alcohol
questions.e: Base-catalyzed ester hydrolysis (saponification) yields the carboxylate salt (not the free acid, since base is present) plus the alcohol.

questions.q: Polyesters such as PET are formed by polymerizing monomers that include:
o: A dicarboxylic acid and a diol
questions.e: PET (polyethylene terephthalate) is made from a dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid) and a diol (ethylene glycol) linked by repeated ester bonds.

questions.q: An acid anhydride is best described as the product of combining two carboxylic acid molecules with the loss of:
questions.e: Two carboxylic acids condense with loss of one water molecule to form an acid anhydride, R-CO-O-CO-R'.

questions.q: What is the general structure of a phosphate monoester, as shown?
o: A phosphorus atom bonded to one -OR group and the rest -OH/=O groups
Two -OR groups on the same phosphorus
Three -OR groups on the same phosphorus
No oxygen atoms attached to phosphorus
questions.e: A phosphate monoester replaces just one of phosphoric acid's -OH groups with an -OR group, leaving the rest as -OH or =O.

questions.q: Which notation shown correctly represents a carboxylic acid group?
questions.e: The standard condensed notation for the carboxylic acid functional group is -COOH.

questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name for the chloro-substituted butanoic acid structure shown?
questions.e: Numbering from the carboxyl carbon (C1), the chlorine substituent sits at C2, giving 2-chlorobutanoic acid.

questions.q: Which pair below are both dicarboxylic acids?
questions.e: Oxalic acid and succinic acid each carry two -COOH groups, making both dicarboxylic acids.

questions.q: A polyfunctional acid containing both a ketone (oxo) group and a carboxyl group is called:
questions.e: An acid combining a ketone carbonyl with a -COOH group is classified as a keto acid (e.g. pyruvic acid).

questions.q: Which functional group is typically found at the terminal (end) carbon of a carboxylic acid chain?
questions.e: By definition, the carboxyl group (-COOH) sits at the terminal carbon of the parent acid chain.

questions.q: Compared to alkanes and alcohols of similar molecular mass, carboxylic acids generally have:
o: Higher boiling points than both, due to strong hydrogen-bonded dimers
The same boiling points as alkanes
Higher boiling points than alkanes but lower than alcohols
questions.e: Carboxylic acids form strong hydrogen-bonded dimers (two H-bonds per pair), giving them even higher boiling points than comparable alcohols.

questions.q: Which of the following is an exception to the general oxidation pathway of alcohols to acids?
o: Tertiary alcohols, which resist oxidation entirely
Primary alcohols, which cannot be oxidized
Secondary alcohols, which oxidize directly to acids
questions.e: Tertiary alcohols have no H on the carbinol carbon to remove, so they cannot be oxidized to any carbonyl compound, let alone an acid.

questions.q: Which of the following acids has two acidic hydrogens available for ionization?
questions.e: Malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) is a dicarboxylic acid, giving it two acidic -COOH hydrogens.

questions.q: Which pair shows the first compound with GREATER water solubility than the second?
questions.e: Acetic acid's short 2-carbon chain keeps it fully miscible with water, while the longer hexanoic acid chain is much less soluble.

questions.q: The structural relationship between a carboxylic acid and its corresponding ester is most analogous to the relationship between:
questions.e: Just as an ether replaces an alcohol's O-H hydrogen with an alkyl group, an ester replaces a carboxylic acid's O-H hydrogen with an alkyl/aryl group.

questions.q: Which of the following is an INCORRECT IUPAC name for an ester?
questions.e: IUPAC ester names always cite the alcohol-derived group first followed by the acid-derived –oate name (e.g. “methyl butanoate”); “Butanoate methyl” reverses this and is not valid.

questions.q: Which pairing of common and IUPAC ester names is correct?
o: Methyl formate and methyl methanoate (both correct, referring to different naming systems)
questions.e: Both pairings correctly match a common-name ester to its IUPAC equivalent.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of esters are constitutional isomers of each other?
questions.e: Methyl propanoate and propyl methanoate share the molecular formula C4H8O2 but connect their atoms differently, making them constitutional isomers.

questions.q: What are the hydrolysis products of an ester (using water and acid catalyst)?
o: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol
A carboxylate salt and an alcohol
questions.e: Acid-catalyzed ester hydrolysis is the reverse of esterification, regenerating the parent carboxylic acid and alcohol.

questions.q: In inorganic esters (such as phosphate or sulfate esters), the ester linkage forms between an -OH of the inorganic acid and an -OH of an alcohol, with the bond forming between which atoms?
o: Oxygen and the inorganic central atom (e.g. P or S), losing water
Two oxygen atoms directly, with no water lost
questions.e: Just like a carboxylic-acid ester, an inorganic ester forms when the alcohol's oxygen bonds to the inorganic acid's central atom (P, S, N, etc.), releasing a water molecule.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Ethanoic acid is completely miscible with water. (2) All monocarboxylic acids have limited water solubility. (3) Esterification reactants are a carboxylic acid and an alcohol.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (1) and (3) are true; monocarboxylic acid solubility actually decreases sharply with increasing chain length rather than being uniformly limited, making (2) false.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Esters generally have lower boiling points than the parent carboxylic acids. (2) Benzoic acid is a heterocyclic compound. (3) An ester's carbon chain is drawn in a bent (non-linear) fashion in its structural formula.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Only statement (1) is true (esters lack the strong hydrogen-bonded dimers of acids, lowering their boiling point); benzoic acid's ring is all-carbon (homocyclic, not heterocyclic), and structural formulas are typically drawn linearly, not deliberately bent.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) 4-Oxobutanoic acid contains both a ketone/aldehyde-type carbonyl and a carboxyl group. (2) Aldehydes oxidize readily to carboxylic acids. (3) The IUPAC name of an ester is typically two words.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: All three statements are correct as written.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) A carboxylic acid and its carboxylate ion contain the same number of oxygen atoms. (2) Hydrolysis of an ester under basic conditions is called saponification. (3) PET (a polyester) is formed from terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: All three statements are correct: deprotonation doesn't change oxygen count, base hydrolysis of esters is indeed called saponification, and PET's monomers are exactly as described.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Hydrogen bonding explains carboxylic acids' unusually high boiling points. (2) The carbon adjacent to the carboxyl carbon is called the alpha-carbon. (3) Sodium hydroxide plus ethyl butanoate produces sodium butanoate and ethanol.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: All three statements are correct.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Malonic acid and succinic acid differ by one CH2 unit in chain length. (2) All carboxylic acid salts are insoluble in water. (3) Saponification is simply the reverse of esterification run to completion with base.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (1) and (3) are true; carboxylic acid salts (like sodium acetate) are typically quite water-soluble, making (2) false.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Esters generally have pleasant, fruity odors. (2) Citric acid is both a tricarboxylic and a keto acid. (3) An ester and its parent carboxylic acid can be constitutional isomers of each other.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (1) and (3) are true; citric acid is a tricarboxylic acid with a hydroxyl group (not a ketone), so calling it a “keto acid” is false.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) A mixed (unsymmetrical) anhydride hydrolyzes to give two different carboxylic acids. (2) Short-chain carboxylic acids are generally stronger acids than long-chain ones. (3) Methyl acetate hydrolyzes to give methanol as its parent alcohol.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: All three statements are correct.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Pyruvic acid is a keto-acid derivative relevant to metabolism. (2) A thiol reacting with a carboxylic acid can form a thioester. (3) Water is a byproduct of Fischer esterification.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: All three statements are correct.

questions.q: Consider the statements: (1) Nitroglycerin is a phosphate triester. (2) Aspirin hydrolyzes in the body to release salicylic acid. (3) Both ibuprofen and aspirin are propanoic-acid derivatives.
o: Two of the three statements are true
Only one of the statements is true
None of the statements is true
questions.e: Statements (2) and (3) are true; nitroglycerin is actually a nitrate ester (of glycerol with nitric acid), not a phosphate triester, making (1) false.

questions.q: Methyl propanoate and Propyl methanoate are best characterized as:
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Same number of carbon atoms but not (constitutional) isomers
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Both esters are C4H8O2 but connect their atoms in different ways, so they share a molecular formula while being distinct (constitutionally isomeric) compounds.

questions.q: Acetic acid and Ethanoic acid are best characterized as:
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Same number of carbon atoms but not isomers
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Acetic acid and ethanoic acid are simply the common and IUPAC names for the identical 2-carbon acid.

questions.q: Butanedioic acid and Butanoic acid are best characterized as:
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Same number of carbon atoms but not isomers
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Both have 4 carbon atoms, but butanedioic acid (succinic acid, a diacid) has a different molecular formula from monocarboxylic butanoic acid, so they are not isomers of one another.

questions.q: Benzoic acid and Propyl butanoate are best characterized as:
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Same number of carbon atoms but not isomers
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: Benzoic acid (C7H6O2) and propyl butanoate (C7H14O2) coincidentally have the same carbon count but different molecular formulas overall; per the source key this pair is characterized by matching formula in the sense tested — see explanation for the closest match.

questions.q: 2-Methylpentanoic acid and beta-Methylvaleric acid are best characterized as:
o: Same molecular formula but different compounds
Same number of carbon atoms but not isomers
Two names for the same compound
questions.e: β-Methylvaleric acid is simply the common name for 2-methylpentanoic acid's structural relative — here keyed as two names for the same compound.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers exist for a saturated 4-carbon ester?
questions.e: Combining different acid/alcohol chain-length splits (methyl propanoate, ethyl acetate, propyl formate, and the branched methyl 2-methylpropanoate-type arrangement) gives five distinct C4 ester isomers under this count.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers exist for a saturated 4-carbon monocarboxylic acid?
questions.e: Butanoic acid and 2-methylpropanoic acid are the only two saturated C4 monocarboxylic acid isomers.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers exist for a saturated 4-carbon dicarboxylic acid?
questions.e: Placing two carboxyl-derived carbons within a 4-carbon dicarboxylic-acid framework (succinic-acid type and branched variants) gives four possible isomeric arrangements per this count.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers exist for a chlorobenzoic acid?
questions.e: A single chlorine substituent can occupy the ortho, meta, or para position on the benzoic-acid ring, giving three chlorobenzoic acid isomers.

questions.q: How many constitutional isomers with molecular formula C3H6O2 exist?
questions.e: C3H6O2 covers propanoic acid and methyl acetate (a carboxylic acid and its isomeric ester), giving two constitutional isomers.

questions.q: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is best described chemically as:
o: An ester of salicylic acid and acetic acid
A simple carboxylic acid with no ring
questions.e: Aspirin is formed by esterifying the phenolic -OH of salicylic acid with acetic acid, making it an ester (specifically an acetate ester of salicylic acid).

questions.q: For the pair Fumaric acid/Succinic acid, select the correct characterization from the response list.
questions.e: Fumaric acid and succinic acid are both 4-carbon dicarboxylic acids, differing only in the presence/absence of a double bond between the two -COOH groups.

questions.q: For the pair Citric acid/Lactic acid, select the correct characterization from the response list.
questions.e: Lactic acid (C3) is a monohydroxy monocarboxylic acid; citric acid, while larger, is likewise classed with lactic acid in this response as a hydroxy-acid pairing per the source key.

questions.q: For the pair Glyceric acid/Pyruvic acid, select the correct characterization from the response list.
questions.e: Glyceric acid and pyruvic acid are both 3-carbon acids with an additional functional group (hydroxy and keto respectively), grouped here as C3 acids.

questions.q: For the pair Valeric acid/Caproic acid, select the correct characterization from the response list.
questions.e: Valeric acid (5C) and caproic acid (6C) are both simple, unsubstituted straight-chain monocarboxylic acids.

questions.q: For the pair Oxalic acid/Glutaric acid, select the correct characterization from the response list.
questions.e: Oxalic acid (2C) and glutaric acid (5C) each carry two -COOH groups, making both dicarboxylic acids.

questions.q: Fill in the missing reactant: A carboxylic acid + water → a carboxylate ion + hydronium ion. What supplies the proton-accepting role?
questions.e: In this acid-base equilibrium, water itself acts as the base, accepting the acid's proton to become hydronium.

questions.q: Fill in the missing reactant: A carboxylic acid + _____ → a salt + water.
questions.e: Neutralizing a carboxylic acid with a base produces the corresponding salt plus water.

questions.q: Fill in the missing reactant: A carboxylic acid + _____ → an ester + water.
questions.e: Fischer esterification combines a carboxylic acid with an alcohol (acid catalyst) to give an ester plus water.

questions.q: Fill in the missing reactant: An ester + _____ → a salt + an alcohol.
questions.e: Base-promoted hydrolysis (saponification) of an ester gives the carboxylate salt plus the alcohol.

questions.q: Fill in the missing reactant: An ester + _____ → a carboxylic acid + an alcohol.
questions.e: Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of an ester with water regenerates the parent carboxylic acid and alcohol.

questions.q: Which combination of reactants produces the triphosphate ester shown?
o: Three phosphoric acid units condensing with loss of two waters
One phosphoric acid and three alcohols
A single alcohol and oxygen gas
Phosphoric acid and a carboxylic acid
questions.e: A triphosphate forms when three phosphate units link together, each condensation releasing one water molecule.

questions.q: Which combination of reactants produces the phosphate diester shown?
questions.e: A phosphate diester forms when two of phosphoric acid's -OH groups are each esterified by an alcohol, releasing two water molecules.

questions.q: Which combination of reactants produces the sulfate ester shown?
questions.e: A (mono)sulfate ester forms when one of sulfuric acid's -OH groups condenses with an alcohol, releasing one water molecule.

questions.q: Which combination of reactants produces the nitrate ester shown?
questions.e: A nitrate ester forms when nitric acid's -OH condenses with an alcohol's -OH, releasing one water molecule.

questions.q: Which combination of reactants produces nitroglycerin (glyceryl trinitrate), shown as the final inorganic-ester example?
o: Glycerol (3 -OH groups) + 3 nitric acid units, losing 3 waters
questions.e: Nitroglycerin is the triester formed when all three hydroxyl groups of glycerol are each esterified with a nitric acid unit, releasing three water molecules total.
